Subject: Clarify uptime baseline & monthly credit cap for batched pilot

Hi Mateo / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the batch inference path looks promising for our nightly enrichment job. Before we go deeper on the pilot, procurement has one ask: can you confirm Redwood's standard availability baseline (we had 99.9% in the slide deck) and the monthly credit calculation if we hit an availability band? Specifically:

- We need a clear credit ladder (percentage of monthly invoice) and a hard cap per month.
- For our use case we will intentionally run a 2-hour high-throughput batch window nightly for the first 90 days — would that be treated as standard load or an exception/carveout?

Leah from procurement is looped in on the thread. If you could send a short addendum (or point to a template) that outlines the matrix and any scheduled-batch carveouts, that would speed approvals.

Thanks,
Alan
Alan Cho
Head of Platform Engineering
ClearStream Health

From: mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@clearstream.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify uptime baseline & monthly credit cap for batched pilot

Alan — thanks for the clear ask. TL;DR: Redwood's standard hosted SLA baseline is 99.9% monthly availability with a three-tier credit ladder; scheduled, notified batch windows can be carved out with advance notice, and we can propose a temporary modification for the pilot quarter. Below is the proposed language we usually send plus a pilot-specific exception.

SLA baseline and monthly credit ladder (proposed):
- Availability >= 99.9%: no credit.
- Availability < 99.9% and >= 99.5%: 10% credit of that month's Redwood service fees.
- Availability < 99.5% and >= 99.0%: 25% credit.
- Availability < 99.0%: 50% credit.
- Credit cap: credits are capped at 100% of that month's fees (one full month max).

Maintenance & scheduled-batch carveout (pilot language):
- If ClearStream notifies Redwood at least 72 hours in advance of a scheduled high-throughput batch window (recurring or one-off), Redwood will treat that window as a scheduled maintenance window for SLA measurement and exclude the window from availability calculations for that billing month, provided the window falls within agreed operational hours and is under an agreed-throughput threshold.
- For the pilot (first 90 days), we can offer to limit the monthly credit cap to 50% (instead of 100%) for incidents attributable to the scheduled batch window, to reduce your procurement's risk.

Carveouts do not apply to unplanned outages or incidents attributable to Redwood platform faults outside the scheduled window. Latency SLOs remain measured separately; if you need explicit p95 numbers for text-generation vs embeddings in pilot mode, tell me target QPS and we will run a targeted perf sweep.

I've attached a short draft addendum and the credit matrix for review. Laura, happy to take your edits before I send to procurement.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sla-addendum-draft.pdf, uptime-credit-matrix.xlsx

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-20T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: internal: pilot carveout framing suggestion

Mateo / Marissa — quick internal note before we send final addendum to ClearStream:

- The 72-hour notice is fine; add a clause that Redwood may request a one-time change to the window (shift by up to 2 hours) for rolling infra maintenance — signal-only, not for every batch.
- For procurement friendliness, make the first-quarter cap 50% as you suggested, but include an automatic review clause at 45 days where we can propose reverting to standard cap (100%) if telemetry shows no elevated incident rate.
- Add explicit latency targets for p95 in the addendum and mark them as "operational targets" (not SLA credits) to avoid double-credit exposure. Example: embeddings p95 <= 75ms at 50 QPS; gen p95 <= 450ms at 10 concurrent streams (pilot-config). We can run a perf sweep once they confirm expected QPS.

I'll mark these in the draft and return.
Laura
VP, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference

From: Alan Cho <alan.cho@clearstream.com>

Thanks Mateo — that layout helps. A few follow-ups from our side: 

1) Leah from procurement confirmed they'd accept the 50% cap for the first 90 days if we have a documented addendum.
2) We need explicit operational p95 targets included in the addendum (as Laura suggested). Procurement prefers targets called "operational commitments" so they are not triggers for credits, but our engineering team will still want them to be binding for performance assessment.
3) Can Redwood include a short runbook excerpt for how incidents during the scheduled batch window are analyzed (timeline to determine attribution)? That helps reduce back-and-forth during post-incident reviews.

If you can send a single PDF addendum with the credit matrix, the carveout text, the operational p95 table, and a 2-paragraph incident attribution runbook, procurement will start redlining. We can loop DocuSign after redlines.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Alan
